concepts.def: Object that gives off its own light.
Object we see by reflected light.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Light is a wave that always travels in straight lines (until something gets in the way).

We draw light paths as rays with arrows showing direction.

In a vacuum, light travels at 300,000,000 m/s - nothing in the universe is faster!

Luminous objects make their own light. Examples: Sun, light bulbs, fires, fireflies.

Non-luminous objects only reflect light from somewhere else. Examples: Moon, you, this screen.

That's why the Moon glows - it reflects the Sun!

When light hits a smooth surface like a mirror, it reflects at the same angle it hit.

Rule: angle of incidence = angle of reflection. Both are measured from the normal (a line at right angles to the surface).

A rough surface scatters light in all directions - we see colour but not a mirror image.

numericals.q: Light hits a mirror at 30 degrees to the normal. What is the angle of reflection in degrees?
